newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields stabilise by close, TWI keeps slipping.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields stabilise by close, TWI keeps slipping.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.55 PCT (PREV 6.50) US 5-YR 6.36 (PREV 6.34) NZD/USD 0.6808/15 (PREV 0.6860/67) US 10-YR 6.49 (PREV 6.45)

New Zealand short rates ended 10 basis points lower in yield on Friday after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised financial markets by endorsing most of the market-led easing that had already occurred.
Markets seized on the RBNZ's six-monthly Monetary Policy Statement with glee, quickly taking conditions another 40 basis points easier than the new assumptions.
Short rates stabilised fairly quickly after the 9.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) release but the kiwi dollar continued to take a hammering late into the session.
The central bank's MPS assumed conditions would be the equivalent of 100 basis points easier during the September quarter than the conditions assumed in the March economic projections.

It saw the Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) averaging 825 in the September quarter, against the 925 level implied by its March assumptions. The market was already extremely close to the desired level at the time of the statement, with the MCI at 824.65. However, the index had shot down to 784.8 by 9.30 a.m.
A 100 point move in the MCI is the same as a 100 basis point move in short rates or a two percent change in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index.
The 90-days ended the week at 6.9 percent, down from 7.02 percent at Thursday's close. The September futures contract ended nine basis points stronger at 93.14, with a solid 6,711 contracts traded.

The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index was still sliding at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT). It was at 66.79, from 67.3 pre-MPS and 67.26 at Thursday's close, and its softness had dragged the MCI even lower, to 779.6.
